issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares orderMeal(Meal) with a void return type, but the solution implements orderMeal(Meal) returning boolean. This is a structural mismatch that may confuse students about the correct method signature they should implement (void vs boolean) and could lead to test or compilation discrepancies if the expected signature differs.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across materials. Either update the problem statement UML and text to specify that orderMeal returns boolean, or change the solution implementation to public void orderMeal(Meal meal) (removing boolean returns) so it matches the UML and instructions.

issues.description: The problem statement first describes the SealSaloon as having a final Stock stock (implying an instance final field) but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute be static (shared across all instances). This is an internal contradiction in the specification. The solution implements the attribute as a static final Stock, which aligns with the later note but contradicts the earlier wording.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification to remove the contradiction: explicitly state that the stock field must be static final (shared across instances). Update the earlier sentence to read e.g. 'a static final Stock stock (shared across all instances)' so it matches the later note and the solution implementation.
